title: Bio-based polymer performance parity
bottleneck: Polymers from biomass could displace petrochemical plastics, but they consistently fall short on the property combinations that matter: PLA is brittle and heat-sensitive, PHA is expensive to ferment at scale, and lignin-based polymers are hard to process reproducibly. Matching the barrier properties, toughness, and thermal stability of polyethylene or PET with a bio-based, biodegradable polymer remains unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Plastics production is a major and growing emissions source, and plastic waste accumulates in the environment. Without performance parity, bio-polymers stay confined to niche packaging while commodity plastics keep expanding.
current_state: PLA and bio-PET have captured meaningful market share in rigid packaging where their limitations are acceptable, and PHA production is scaling. But for films, engineering parts, and hot-fill applications, petrochemical polymers still have no bio-based rival.
